An assessment can then establish the cause, the repair options and which checks are appropriate before work is proposed.Washing Machine Repair / assessmentILLUSTRATIVEInlet, drainage and hose checksDrum, motor and control assessmentWash-cycle and leak testing01 / DRAINAGEWater stays inside after washingExplain whether the machine stops before spinning, whether water remains visible and whether a display message appears. pages.mainText: Back to Repair GuidesShareLaptop faults:repair or replace?No power, overheating and slow storage have different causes. Use the fault, device condition and repair scope to decide what is worth doing.READ ARTICLEALL REPAIR GUIDESNumunix Repair TeamNovember 1, 20266 min read6 sectionsElectronicsRepair assessmentAftercareTable of ContentsNEED HELP?Tell us the model and symptoms to discuss a repair assessment.Get in touch Table of Contents01Separate a fault from an upgrade requestA laptop that starts slowly is different from one that shuts down under load. Note startup behaviour, fan noise, heat, battery performance and any screen or keyboard issues. Share the model and recent impact or liquid exposure. Avoid treating every slow device as a storage upgrade until existing hardware condition has been reviewed.02When power and display need assessmentNo visible picture does not always mean a broken screen. The adapter, battery, power path, display connection or board may be involved. Describe whether lights or fans start and whether an external display has already been used. Do not dismantle a damaged charger or repeatedly power on a laptop after liquid exposure.03Think about files before hardware workBack up important files when the laptop can still run. If storage is unreadable, stop unnecessary use and discuss recovery separately. Explain which files matter, but do not send passwords in a form. Confirm whether a repair might require storage removal, operating-system work or further access for testing.YOUR REPAIR, YOUR DECISIONNeed a repair assessment?Share the model, symptoms and location. Review the options and estimate before approving work.REQUEST ASSESSMENT04Compare the whole repair with replacementConsider the assessed fault, compatible parts, overall condition, battery and screen health, and the tasks you need the laptop to perform. A practical repair can preserve a useful device, while a large repair on several failing parts may be less sensible. Ask for alternatives and an estimate that separates required repairs from optional upgrades.05Test the everyday work you rely onAt handover, review power, charging, keyboard, display, cooling and storage recognition as relevant to the work. Ask whether intermittent faults were reproduced and under what conditions the device was tested.
